speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an infant presenting with recurrent stridor and wheezing, particularly during specific activities. To begin our examination, can you describe exactly what activities seem to trigger these breathing difficulties?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a concerning combination of symptoms. The vomiting after feeding and worsening of stridor with neck flexion are particularly notable; have you noticed any recurrent "choking" episodes where the child seems to inhale food or liquid into their airway?

text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.
